newsitem.title: USA: Democrats got $27 mln from coffee guests - report.
newsitem.headline: Democrats got $27 mln from coffee guests - report.

text.p: The Democratic Party received $27 million over two years from guests who attended coffee chats at the White House, the Los Angeles Times reported on Tuesday.

A computer analysis done for the newspaper showed that many of those who attended the affairs with President Bill Clinton or administration officials "made substantial contributions to the Democratic Party within days of the events."
The White House has defended the coffee chats as appropriate, exposing Clinton to various views, and has denied the events were designed to solicit funds.

"The pattern of donations suggests, however, that the 103 meetings between January 1995 and August 1996 were part of a system that cultivated major supporters who, in many cases, gave large contributions before or after attending the White House events," the Times said.
It said the records raised new questions about whether the Democratic National Committee used the White House and personal audiences with Clinton as part of a fund-raising programme.

Congressional hearings are planned into fund-raising practices, primarily by Democrats, that have been highly controversial, including collecting money from foreigners or people associated with foreign interests.

The Times said a computer analysis done for the paper by Campaign Study Group of Springfield, Virginia, "found that the Democrats collected $27,018,553 in 'soft money' contributions from 358 people invited to meet with Clinton."
Soft money is given to parties for party-building, get-out-the-vote and educational purposes without the strict limits on donations given directly to candidates.

The newspaper noted it was not illegal for a president to meet with supporters but it said critics have charged that the large number of coffee chats left the impression that the White House was put up for sale.
